summary: Iteration 33 — MIXED. Backend PASS 6/6 (task end_time round-trip via POST/GET/PATCH, invoice PDF regression still 200 application/pdf, unauth still 401). Frontend PASS on Business Settings save-lifecycle (save button HIDDEN on load / VISIBLE after edit / green settings-saved-badge briefly then settings-clean pill), Shift screen (Save to planner + Start now buttons both present, schedule-date input removed), Planner new-task modal (task-start-input auto-formats '0900'→'09:00', task-end-input '1730'→'17:30', task-duration-hint reads 'Shift duration: 8h 30m'). FRONTEND CRITICAL BUG: the new in-app invoice preview screen (/invoice/preview/[id].tsx) NEVER finishes loading — screen is stuck on the ActivityIndicator, invoice-preview-screen testID never mounts, footer buttons preview-close-btn/preview-download-btn never appear, no paper mock renders (verified over 7 s wait, and repeated via both preview-invoice-btn tap and direct URL navigation). Backend calls succeed independently (GET /api/invoices/{id} 200 in 96 ms, GET /api/auth/me 200 in 156 ms) so this is a pure client-side rendering issue. Root cause = anti-pattern in /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/invoice/preview/[id].tsx:45 — `if (loading && !inv) load();` invoked during render, which triggers setState inside render and re-enters load() on every render, preventing the promise from ever settling into the ‘data ready’ branch. Fix: move to `useEffect(() => { load(); }, [load]);`. Everything downstream of the preview (Share PDF from footer, sections, meta grid) could not be exercised because the screen never renders. Deprecated packages: none.

critical_code_review_comments: /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/invoice/preview/[id].tsx:45 — `if (loading && !inv) load();` is a React anti-pattern. Calling an async function that setState during render body triggers infinite re-renders and prevents the completion state from being observed by React’s reconciler. rca_of_issue: Preview stuck-loading RCA: /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/invoice/preview/[id].tsx line 45 uses `if (loading && !inv) load();` as a render-body fetcher. React re-renders the component after any setState call inside `load` (setLoading(true), then setInv, then setLoading(false)). Because the fetcher is called from render (not an effect), React can enter a render loop that never surfaces the resolved state to the DOM. Fix: swap to `useEffect(() => { load(); }, [load]);` (or `useFocusEffect(useCallback(() => { load(); }, [load]));` if you want a re-fetch on focus). No backend or auth work required — proven by curl round-trip to GET /api/invoices/{id} completing in <100 ms.
